newsitem.title: USA: Alaska governor signs bill lifting jet-fuel tax.
newsitem.headline: Alaska governor signs bill lifting jet-fuel tax.

text.p: Saying it will help in-state refineries and possibly attract more international air service, Alaska Gov. Tony Knowles Monday signed a bill that eliminates a state tax on jet fuel used for certain international flights.
The bill removes the state's 3.2-cent-per-gallon tax on aviation fuel sold at the Anchorage and Fairbanks international airports, both foreign trade zones.

Under federal law, jet fuel shipped into those foreign trade zones has been exempted from state taxes. Knowles said it was necessary to remove the state tax to allow Alaska refinerers to compete fairly with companies barging fuel up to the state.
With the bill "leveling the playing field, in-state refiners are likely to expand their operations and create more jobs for Alaskans," Knowles, a Democrat, said in a news release.
The bill, passed in May by the Republican-controlled state legislature, may also attract regular airline passenger service between Japan and Alaska, Knowles said.

"Potential jet fuel customers -- FedEx, All Nippon Airways, Northwest Airlines, to name a few -- say a more friendly Alaska business climate will encourage them to increase international operations here in Alaska and perhaps resume direct air passenger service between Alaska and Japan," he said.
The bill also grants a tax exemption for alcohol-based fuel produced from wood chips and seafood waste -- production that has not yet occurred in Alaska.

It eliminates a tax exemption for ethanol-blended gasoline sold in Anchorage. Under the bill, the exemption for state taxes on gasohol would remain in place only during the four winter months when its use is mandated by the federal Clean Air Act.
